correctness.rationale: The horoball y>=1 is hyperbolically geodesically convex, so intrinsic shortest paths on the quotient select the nearest horizontal deck translate. With normalized area, H_i=log y_i iid Exp(1); S=|H1-H2|~Exp(1), M=min(H_i)~Exp(2), independently, and circular displacement W=2|Δ|/λ~Uniform(0,1). U=e^{-2M} is independent Uniform(0,1), giving cosh D=cosh S+(λ²/8)e^{-S} UW² and P(UW²>z)=(1-sqrt z)². Conditioning on S gives the claimed full-r integral. The Laplace endpoint near s=r has width λ² e^{-2r}/4 and integral ∫0^1(1-sqrt t)²dt=1/6, giving e^-r+λ² e^-3r/24+O_λ(e^-5r); coupling proves strict width stochastic order. Independently compared the new full-r integral numerically against the older exact cusp formula at λ=.3,1,4 and radii .5,2,6; adaptive quadrature with endpoint breakpoints agreed to about 6e-14, confirming equality, not novelty.
